CODE OF BUSINESS CONDUCT AND ETHICS

Thornapple Instruments Corporation
Adopted by the Board of Directors on January 21, 2026

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This Code of Business Conduct and Ethics states the standards of conduct expected of everyone who acts for Thornapple Instruments Corporation. It applies to every director, officer, and employee of the Company and of each of its subsidiaries, worldwide, and it applies to contractors, consultants, and agents when they act on the Company's behalf. It is adopted under Section 303A.10 of the NYSE Listed Company Manual and is intended to satisfy Section 406 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and Item 406 of Regulation S-K.

No code can address every situation. Where this Code is silent, use judgment, and ask before you act. If a local law is stricter than this Code, follow the local law. If a local custom conflicts with this Code, follow this Code.

2. HONEST AND ETHICAL CONDUCT

Every director, officer, and employee shall act with honesty, integrity, and ethical conduct, including the ethical handling of actual or apparent conflicts of interest between personal and professional relationships. You may not take unfair advantage of anyone through manipulation, concealment, abuse of privileged information, or misrepresentation of material facts.

3. FULL, FAIR, AND ACCURATE DISCLOSURE

The Company is committed to full, fair, accurate, timely, and understandable disclosure in the reports and documents it files with or submits to the Securities and Exchange Commission and in its other public communications. The Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, the Controller, and every employee who participates in the preparation of those reports shall take all steps reasonably within their control to that end. No one may take any action to fraudulently influence, coerce, manipulate, or mislead the Company's independent auditors.

4. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS, RULES, AND REGULATIONS

The Company requires compliance with all laws, rules, and regulations that apply to its business, including the securities laws, competition and antitrust laws, export control and sanctions laws, environmental and workplace safety laws, employment and anti-discrimination laws, and the anti-corruption laws of every country in which the Company operates. You must comply with the laws, regulations, and rules of every jurisdiction in which you act for the Company.

5. CONFLICTS OF INTEREST

A conflict of interest arises when your private interest interferes, or appears to interfere, with the interests of the Company. You shall disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest to the Chief Compliance Officer promptly. Outside employment with a competitor, customer, or supplier, service on the board of another for-profit company, and any financial interest in a competitor, customer, or supplier other than a holding of less than one percent (1%) of a public company's securities require prior written approval. A related-party transaction involving a director or an executive officer requires approval by the Audit Committee.

6. GIFTS AND ENTERTAINMENT

You may give or accept business courtesies of modest value that are customary, infrequent, and not intended to influence a decision. You may not give or accept cash or a cash equivalent, and you may not give anything of value to a government official without prior approval from the Legal Department. Any gift or entertainment exceeding $250 in value must be reported to the Chief Compliance Officer within ten (10) business days.

7. CORPORATE OPPORTUNITIES, CONFIDENTIALITY, AND COMPANY ASSETS

You may not take for yourself an opportunity discovered through your position or through the use of Company property or information, use Company property or information for personal gain, or compete with the Company. You shall maintain the confidentiality of information entrusted to you by the Company or by its customers and suppliers, except where disclosure is authorized or legally required. You shall protect Company assets against loss, theft, and misuse.

8. FAIR DEALING

Each director, officer, and employee shall deal fairly with the Company's customers, suppliers, competitors, and employees, and shall not take unfair advantage of anyone through manipulation, concealment, abuse of privileged information, misrepresentation of material facts, or any other unfair dealing practice.

9. REPORTING VIOLATIONS

If you know of or suspect a violation of this Code, of law, or of Company policy, report it. You may report to your manager, to the Legal Department, to the Chief Compliance Officer, or through the Company's Integrity Helpline, which is operated by an independent third party, is available in every language in which the Company operates, is available at all hours, and permits you to report anonymously where local law allows.

Concerns regarding accounting, internal accounting controls, or auditing matters are referred directly to the Audit Committee under the procedures the Audit Committee has adopted under Section 301 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.

10. NON-RETALIATION

The Company prohibits retaliation against anyone who in good faith reports a suspected violation, raises a concern, or participates in an investigation. Retaliation is itself a violation of this Code and is grounds for discipline up to and including termination. Nothing in this Code, and nothing in any Company agreement or policy, limits your right to report a possible violation of law to a government agency or regulator, to cooperate with an investigation, or to receive an award under a whistleblower program, and you do not need the Company's permission or need to tell the Company before you do so.

11. INVESTIGATIONS AND DISCIPLINE

The Chief Compliance Officer, or the Audit Committee for matters within its charter, shall cause each report to be investigated promptly and, where appropriate, by counsel independent of the business unit involved. Violations of this Code may result in discipline up to and including termination of employment, and may be referred to law enforcement.

12. WAIVERS AND AMENDMENTS

A waiver of any provision of this Code for a director or an executive officer may be granted only by the Board of Directors or a committee of the Board. Any such waiver, and any amendment of this Code that applies to a director or an executive officer, shall be disclosed on a Form 8-K within four business days of the waiver or amendment, or by any other means the New York Stock Exchange and the SEC then permit. A waiver for any other employee may be granted only by the Chief Compliance Officer.

13. ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND ADMINISTRATION

Each director, officer, and employee shall acknowledge in writing, on hire and annually thereafter, that they have read and understand this Code. The Chief Compliance Officer administers this Code and reports on compliance to the Audit Committee at least annually. Questions about this Code should be directed to the Chief Compliance Officer at compliance@thornappleinstruments.com or to the Integrity Helpline.
